This is the game: you're always one step behind having it together, and once you DO get it together, the storyteller blindsides you. If heat is an issue and the electric is down you can use passive coolers (it's a tier 1 research, takes about a day, but you'd need to start on it before the problem), forbid the freezer so pawns don't go in and out and let the heat in (open doors bleed). Hats are a fast-to-make and very effective heat blocker. Be prepared to lose ALL your meat at any time, but animal corpses last longer than butchered meat, and harvested vegetables last forever in the heat. If you know you can't handle an event, pack up a caravan & load everything up... you're better off heading out to sell the meat than having it all spoil (meat weighs like nothing). Always use the buddy system or send your caravan with a pet (they can and will be ambushed and you can not run). You can always pick berries if it gets bad. Also, it's kind of cheating, but I always put my colony directly bordering an ally, the round trip is about 1.6 hours, so I can trade for a one-off resource. Ultimately, 90% of the game is knowing (ahead of time) what COULD possibly go wrong, and planning for things that haven't yet happened. I always keep a couple medicines handy even if no one is sick, and build 2 coolers for my freezer even though one will do the job. I build heaters when I don't need them (just in case of a cold snap). Still, every game I get blindsided by something. We're all just kind of doin stuff, a lot of us have bad judgement a lot of the time, and a lot of us are good people that do dumb things.
